title: FARCO 88 Corn (Farco 88W): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: FARCO 88 Corn: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: FARCO 88 corn is a yellow hybrid corn variety for Mindanao. About 106 days to harvest, 6.3 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits.
excerpt: FARCO 88 corn is a yellow hybrid corn variety, also sold or known as Farco 88W. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2020 as NSIC 2020 Cn 329. Fareast Agricultural Seeds Multipurpose Cooperative bred it. It takes about 106 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain, with 6.34 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Farco 88W, this is the same corn. Its seller and farm sources add notes, listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [corn variety finder](/crop-varieties/corn), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Pagtatanim ng mais, step by step](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-mais).

items: **Days to harvest:** about 106 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain.
**Yield:** 6.34 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

FARCO 88 corn takes about 106 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain. That is about the average of the 215 yellow hybrid corn varieties with a day count, 103.6 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 6.34 t/ha trails the average of its group, 7.17. It sits in the lower quarter of its group. One tonne of shelled corn fills about 20 sacks of 50 kilograms. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit corn fields most often: [Asian corn borer](/pests/asian-corn-borer), [banded leaf and sheath blight](/diseases/banded-leaf-and-sheath-blight), [Corn downy mildew](/diseases/corn-downy-mildew), [Corn ear rot](/diseases/corn-ear-rot), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Its ears grew about 15.5 cm long in the trials. The shelling recovery was 79.77 percent, the share of the ear weight that comes off as grain. A higher share means more grain from every sack of ears.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** DA 12 trials: 5.66 t/ha Sultan Kudarat highland, 4.84 t/ha Sarangani lowland, 3.23 t/ha Sarangani highland.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: second in the white hybrid class in three DA 12 trials, 2024 to 2025. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant FARCO 88 corn

It is recommended for Mindanao. Start with the color your buyer pays for: yellow corn goes to feed mills, while white and glutinous corn go to the table. Next, pick between a hybrid, which yields more but needs new seed every season, and an open pollinated variety, whose seed you can save. Then match the island group in its recommendation, because trials in Luzon and Mindanao give different winners. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for corn](/land-preparation/corn-land-preparation).

items.q: Is Farco 88W the same as FARCO 88?
items.a: Yes. Farco 88W is another name for FARCO 88, registered as NSIC 2020 Cn 329. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 106 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 6.34 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.
It is recommended for Mindanao. Ask your municipal agriculturist how it has done in your town.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of FARCO 88?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
